newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian Moslems attack churches, temples.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian Moslems attack churches, temples.

text.p: A mob of Indonesian Moslems burned and wrecked churches and temples east of Jakarta on Thursday after reports that a Christian had insulted Moslems, officials and eyewitnesses said.
"The rampage was sparked by an (ethnic) Chinese woman who scolded a number of youths for being too noisy," Dadang Muchtar, the head of the Karawang regency, told a news conference.

He said the youths were beating drums to wake Moslems in the neighbourhood early on Thursday so they could eat before fasting through the day. The Moslem fasting month of Ramadan ends at sunset on February 8.
Dadang said the mob wrecked five churches and a Chinese temple in this small town in a rice-growing area 50 km (30 miles) east of Jakarta. He said 16 cars were also set ablaze.
He said there were no injuries, and eyewitnesses said the town was quiet but tense after troops and riot police moved in to patrol the streets.
"Four people have been arrested after the disturbance," Dadang said, adding that the Chinese woman was one of those detained. He gave no other details.
Eyewitnesses said a Pentecostal church, another church and a temple had been burned down.
The caretaker at the Pentecostal church told Reuters: "They came in two groups. The first group came and wrecked the place. The second group came with petrol and burned it."
He said his home and the pastor's house behind the church were also ransacked and wrecked.
Eyewitnesses said a number of shops were damaged and looted, including a jewellery store which had been emptied after its door was smashed in.
The owners of some homes and shops had written "Moslem, don't touch" on the walls to protect them.
Some members of the mob had scrawled graffiti on walls saying "Moslem power", "Long live Islam", and "Destroy the Chinese".
Ethnic Chinese, a number of whom are Christians and are regarded as more wealthy in their neighbourhoods, are frequently targets of mob violence in Indonesia.

Eyewitnesses said the mob, shouting "Allahu Akbar" (God is Greatest) attacked the churches in the morning. "They smashed the windows, music instruments and also the Bible," said one church attendant whose church was damaged.
Last month, four people died when a mob went on a rampage in the town of Tasikmalaya in West Java, setting fire to shops, buildings and churches.
That riot was sparked by reports of police brutality towards a Moslem religious teacher.

Political and social analysts have blamed the eruptions of violence on socio-economic tensions. Some government members have said they believed there was a Maoist conspiracy involved but have provided no proof of this.
